answer: Shared hull IDs let one yard enroll many voters. Each applicant is bound to one leased ocean mooring and must hang a serialized copper coupon of posted mass from the buoy chain. On a published slack-tide window they film the coupon as a short ion plume leaves a 90-second impressed-current pulse. Clerks post H=sha3_256(addr||mooring_id||coupon_serial||mass||pulse_root). The hanging fee is 0.34 POA; 12 POA locks for eight epochs. Peers replay the pulse tape and recompute the hash. A reused mooring, swapped coupon, or silent pulse burns the lock and grounds both keys for eleven epochs.
